title: Cohen rings exist
statement: Let $p$ be a prime number and $k$ a field of characteristic $p$. Then there exist a Cohen ring $\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring] (a discrete valuation ring whose maximal ideal is $p\Lambda$ and which is $p\Lambda$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]) and a ring isomorphism $\Lambda/p\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}k$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328 (lemma-cohen-rings-exist, line 44878) and its proof (lines 44885-44910); Cohen ring: Definition Tag 0327 (definition-cohen-ring, line 44872)

proof.text: (The base ring $\mathbf Z_p$ and the residue field extension.) Let $\mathbf Z_p$ be the ring of $p$-adic integers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] (with $\ell=p$): a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $p\mathbf Z_p$ (so $p\neq0$ in $\mathbf Z_p$, $\mathbf Z_p$ is a domain and a local ring, and it is Noetherian, every ideal being principal) with $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p\cong\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$ for all $n\ge1$; in particular its residue field is $\mathbf Z_p/p\mathbf Z_p\cong\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$. Since $k$ has characteristic $p$, the kernel of the unique ring map $\mathbf Z\to k$ is $p\mathbf Z$, so it induces a ring homomorphism $\mathbf F_p\to k$; composing with $\mathbf Z_p/p\mathbf Z_p\cong\mathbf F_p$ makes $k$ a field extension of the residue field of $\mathbf Z_p$. (The source notes first that $\mathbf Z_p$ is a Cohen ring for $\mathbf F_p$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328, proof, first two sentences

proof.text: (A flat local $\mathbf Z_p$-algebra $R$ with $\mathfrak m_R=pR$ and $R/pR\cong k$.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-extension-given-residue-field] to the local ring $\mathbf Z_p$ (maximal ideal $p\mathbf Z_p$, residue field $\mathbf F_p$) and the extension $k/\mathbf F_p$ of step 1: there are a local ring $R$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_R$, a flat local ring map $\mathbf Z_p\to R$ with $\mathfrak m_R=p\mathbf Z_pR=pR$, and an isomorphism of fields $R/pR=R/\mathfrak m_R\xrightarrow{\sim}k$. In particular $R/pR$ is a field and $pR\neq R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328, proof, 'Let Z_p -> R be a flat local ring map such that m_R = pR and R/pR = k, see Lemma 03C3'

proof.text: (The completion $\Lambda$: Noetherian, $p\Lambda$-adically complete, $\Lambda/p\Lambda\cong k$.) Let $\Lambda=R^\wedge=\varprojlim_nR/p^nR$ be the $pR$-adic completion of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], with canonical map $\iota:R\to\Lambda$; it is a $\mathbf Z_p$-algebra through $\mathbf Z_p\to R\to\Lambda$, and $(pR)\Lambda=p\Lambda$. The ideal $pR$ is generated by one element, and $R/pR\cong k$ is a field, hence Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] (its only ideals are $0$ and the whole ring). By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] (with $I=pR$) $\Lambda$ is a Noetherian ring. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (with $A=R$, $I=pR$ finitely generated) $\Lambda$ is $p\Lambda$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], and the map $\Lambda\to R/pR$, $(x_n)_n\mapsto x_1$, is surjective with kernel $p\Lambda$, so it induces an isomorphism $\Lambda/p\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R/pR$; composing with step 2 gives a ring isomorphism $\varepsilon:\Lambda/p\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}k$. In particular $\Lambda/p\Lambda$ is a field, so $p\Lambda$ is a maximal ideal of $\Lambda$ and $\Lambda\neq0$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328, proof, 'By Lemma 05GH the completion Lambda = R^ is Noetherian. Since Lambda/pLambda = R/pR is a field ... (equality and completeness by Lemma 05GG)'

proof.text: ($\Lambda$ is local with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$.) Since $\Lambda$ is $p\Lambda$-adically complete (step 3), [lem-weil-pbc-adic-complete-jacobson-radical] gives that every maximal ideal $\mathfrak M$ of $\Lambda$ contains $p\Lambda$. As $p\Lambda$ is itself maximal (step 3), $\mathfrak M=p\Lambda$. So $\Lambda$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda$; equivalently, every element of $\Lambda\setminus p\Lambda$ is a unit (it lies in no maximal ideal).

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328, proof, 'we conclude Lambda is a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal (p)'

proof.text: ($\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\cong R/p^nR$ for every $n\ge1$.) Fix $n\ge1$ and let $R^{\wedge,n}=\varprojlim_mR/p^{nm}R$ be the $p^nR$-adic completion of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. The map $\theta:\Lambda\to R^{\wedge,n}$, $(x_m)_m\mapsto(x_{nm})_m$, is a ring isomorphism compatible with the canonical maps from $R$: its inverse sends $(y_m)_m$ to $(x_m)_m$ with $x_m$ the image of $y_m$ under $R/p^{nm}R\to R/p^mR$ (well defined as $nm\ge m$; compatibility of the families is checked componentwise, and the two composites are the identity because $x_m$ is the image of $x_{nm}$). Hence $\theta$ is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras and carries $p^n\Lambda$ onto $(p^nR)R^{\wedge,n}=p^nR^{\wedge,n}$. The ideal $p^nR$ is generated by one element, so [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (with $A=R$, $I=p^nR$) gives an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $R^{\wedge,n}/p^nR^{\wedge,n}\xrightarrow{\sim}R/p^nR$, $(y_m)_m\mapsto y_1$. Composing: $\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}R/p^nR$, $(x_m)_m\mapsto x_n$, an isomorphism of $R$-algebras, hence of $\mathbf Z_p$-modules.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328, proof, 'Lambda/p^nLambda = R/p^nR (equality by Lemma 05GG again)'

proof.text: ($\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is flat over $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p\cong\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$.) The ring map $\mathbf Z_p\to R$ is flat (step 2), so by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-base-change] (base change along $\mathbf Z_p\to\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p$) the module $(\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_p}R$ is flat over $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. By right exactness of $-\otimes_{\mathbf Z_p}R$ applied to $\mathbf Z_p\xrightarrow{p^n}\mathbf Z_p\to\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p\to0$, this module is $R/p^nR$, with its $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p$-module structure induced from $\mathbf Z_p\to R$. By step 5, $\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\cong R/p^nR$ as $\mathbf Z_p$-modules, hence as $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p$-modules (both are killed by $p^n$). So $\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is flat over $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p\cong\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$ for every $n\ge1$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 0328, proof, 'For every n the map Z/p^nZ -> Lambda/p^nLambda = R/p^nR is flat'

proof.text: ($\mathbf Z_p\to\Lambda$ is flat.) Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-module-powers] to the ring map $\mathbf Z_p\to\Lambda$, the ideal $I=p\mathbf Z_p$ and the $\Lambda$-module $M=\Lambda$: (1) $\mathbf Z_p$ is Noetherian (step 1); (2) $\Lambda$ is Noetherian (step 3); (3) $\Lambda$ is a finitely generated $\Lambda$-module (by $1$); (4) $M/I^nM=\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is flat over $\mathbf Z_p/p^n\mathbf Z_p$ for all $n\ge1$ (step 6). Since $\Lambda$ is local with maximal ideal $p\Lambda=I\Lambda$ (step 4), the last assertion of that lemma gives that $\Lambda$ is a flat $\mathbf Z_p$-module.
